evidence.note: Built test_full.py explicitly for 'Full domain correctness' — a grid-wide correctness ledger rather than single-shape eyeballing.
Wrote bench.py to 'Benchmark 10 latency shapes'; re-ran it after nearly every kernel change (121,151,322,432,484,514,530,601,630), maintaining running latency status vs the gate.
Repeated per-stage profiling of the largest shapes (N=2048, dim=384), identifying the binding worst-case shape and the bottleneck stage that gates the max-of-10 score.

Fused onorm+final change → 'Find failing cases' → 'Verify revert and benchmark': caught a correctness regression from an optimization and rolled it back, i.e. detecting when a fix for one thing broke another.

Very large volume of repeated bmm config sweeps interleaved with re-profiling; shows sustained focus on the bottleneck but borders on circular re-tuning, which keeps it below the level-10 anchor of clear stuck-state detection/reallocation.

reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit correctness harness across the full domain (ref/fp64 oracles + test_full.py) and a 10-shape latency benchmark that it re-ran after edits, repeatedly profiled the binding largest shapes to locate the gating bottleneck, and caught at least one cross-case regression (fused onorm+final broke correctness, then reverted) — matching the level-8 description of an explicit correctness+latency ledger with regression detection and worst-case identification. It falls short of 10 because the dozens of repeated bmm sweeps suggest possible circular re-tuning without visible evidence (in this description-only log) of detecting the stuck state and deliberately reallocating effort.
